review_question: Does synthetic multi-view consistency provide instance-discriminative connectivity for overlap resolution?

protocol.criterion: clean H0/V0 within != cross c_mv, and H1/V1 (where cross edges exist) within > cross with margin >= 0.03

clean_levels_have_zero_cross_edges.meaning: clean selectivity guard is vacuous on clean levels; the real test is H1/V1

visibility_coverage.conclusion: K=2 transmittance raises coverage but does not restore discriminability

root_cause: Synthetic orbit cameras re-project the existing static splat cloud; no new information is introduced. 62-74% of a/b gaussians are visible in 0 views under either visibility model, so c_vis/c_app collapse to 0 for BOTH within-leaf and cross-leaf edges (both co-visibility sets are tiny). c_occ saturates to ~1.0 because neither endpoint is visible -> no occlusion separation to score. The remaining 0.3 'signal' is the constant c_occ contribution, identical within and cross.
conclusion: STOP per plan: no parameter grid. View-synthesized evidence from a static 3DGS cloud cannot provide instance-discriminative connectivity for this benchmark. This matches the plan's designed honest-FAIL gate: 'no real cameras/images, synthetic multi-view itself cannot produce sufficient instance info'. Next stage must introduce real captured images / 2D multi-view instance cues rather than squeeze more from the PLY.
task3_parallel: G4 surface gate also failed (c_t within~cross at V0); G6 identity gate fails the same way at H1/V1. Both confirm overlap failures are not due to insufficient local geometry estimation.
